Flag the routeable flowlines (the routing network)

Source: R/flag_routeable_flowlines.R
flag_routeable_flowlines.Rd

Adds a logical routeable attribute to the flowlines layer marking the reaches in the routing network: the flowpath-constituent (coincident) flowlines plus the incremental reaches that bridge a coincident flowline to the next coincident flowline downstream. Routing follows the native flowline_toid; the routeable == TRUE subgraph is closed under it (every non-terminal routeable flowline drains to a routeable flowline), so a consumer can route on the routeable set without a coincident reach draining into a non-coincident connector that is filtered out ("flying water").

A bridge reach is a real channel carrying flow between mainstems; it is non-coincident only because aggregation traced a different mainstem. When a coincident flowline never rejoins a coincident flowline downstream, the bridge is extended to the terminal instead, so the reach's flow exits the domain rather than draining into a filtered-out connector.

Requires flowpath_constituent on the flowlines layer (see flag_flowpath_constituents(), which must run first).

Usage

flag_routeable_flowlines(input_gpkg, flowlines_layer = "flowlines")

Arguments

input_gpkg

Path to a GeoPackage containing flowlines_layer.

flowlines_layer

Layer name. Default "flowlines".

Value

Invisibly, the number of routeable flowlines. Adds routeable (logical) to flowlines_layer, overwriting it in place.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
flag_routeable_flowlines("ngen_vpu01.gpkg")
} # }
